# std.segtree

Segment tree over a domain, for any associative operation: point or range update, range query.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `SegTree`.

- `fn apply(mut self, r: Range<D>, f: F)` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); Apply tag `f` to every position of `r`: each fold over `r` then sees the values with `f` applied, through the action given to `act:`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn apply_all(mut self, f: F)` — \(O(1)\) amortized when the tags commute, else \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\); Apply tag `f` to every position; `apply(D.all, f)`.
- `fn fold(self, r: Range<D>) -> T` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); The fold of the values in `r`, left to right: `op(op(a[l], a[l + 1]), ...)`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn right_while(self, from: Cut<D>, ok: T -> Bool) -> Cut<D>` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); The last cut `d` at or right of `from` such that `ok(fold(from..d))` holds.; traps: when `ok(identity)` is false

- `fn of<M>(op: M, f: D -> T) -> SegTree<D, T, F>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\), calling `f` once per position in key order; A tree whose position `i` holds `f(i)`.
- `fn refresh(mut self, i: D)` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) plus one call of `f`; Recompute position `i` as `f(i)` with the formula given to `of`, and update its ancestors.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`, or the tree was not built with `of`
- `fn get(self, i: D) -> T` — \(O(1)\); \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) on a tree with `act:`; The value at position `i`, with every tag applied.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `fn set(mut self, i: D, x: T)` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); Make position `i` hold `x`, replacing any tags applied to it, and update its ancestors.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `fn at(mut self, i: D) -> lends mut T` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) per write; Position `i` as a writable place: `st.at(i) += x`, `st.at(i) max= x`.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`

- `fn new(a: [D]T) -> MergeSortTree<D, T>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert \log \lvert D \rvert)\) time and memory; A static tree over `a` whose nodes hold their values sorted, for counting values in a range.

- `fn count_gt(self, r: Range<D>, x: T) -> Int` — \(O(\log^2 \lvert D \rvert)\); The number of positions in `r` whose value is `> x`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`

- `fn first_ge(self, r: Range<D>, x: T) -> ?T` — \(O(\log^2 \lvert D \rvert)\); The smallest value in `r` that is `>= x`, or `None`.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`

## `struct MergeSeg<D>`

One set of positions of `D` in a `MergeSegs<D>` pool: a handle, so copying it is O(1).

## `struct MergeSegs<D>`

A pool of mergeable sets of positions of `D`, each stored as a sparse binary segment tree whose nodes the sets share.

- `fn singleton(mut self, x: D) -> MergeSeg<D>` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) time and new nodes; The set holding only `x`.
- `fn merge(mut self, a: MergeSeg<D>, b: MergeSeg<D>) -> MergeSeg<D>` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) amortized per position, over a sequence of merges whose; The union of `a` and `b`.
- `fn first_alive(mut self, mut s: MergeSeg<D>, alive: D -> Bool) -> ?D` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) amortized; The smallest position `x` in `s` with `alive(x)`, or `None`.
- `fn first_ge(self, s: MergeSeg<D>, x: D) -> ?D` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); The smallest position of `s` at or after `x`, or `None`.
- `fn any_in(self, s: MergeSeg<D>, r: Range<D>) -> Bool` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); Whether `s` holds a position in `r`.

## `struct MergeTree<D>`

## `struct MergeTrees<D, Z: Add + Mul>`

A pool of sparse segment trees over `D` holding values `Z`, each with a whole-tree multiply tag.

Fields: `ls: List<Int>`, `rs: List<Int>`, `sm: List<Z>`, `tag: List<Z>`.

- `fn new() -> MergeTrees<D, Z>` — \(O(1)\); An empty pool.
- `fn set(mut self, mut t: MergeTree<D>, x: D, v: Z)` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) time and new nodes; Sets position `x` of `t` to `v`.
- `fn sum(self, t: MergeTree<D>, r: Range<D>) -> Z` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); The sum of `t` over the positions in `r`.
- `fn get(self, t: MergeTree<D>, x: D) -> Z` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\); The value of `t` at `x`.
- `fn total(self, t: MergeTree<D>) -> Z` — \(O(1)\); The sum of every value of `t`.
- `fn scale(mut self, t: MergeTree<D>, k: Z)` — \(O(1)\); Multiplies every value of `t` by `k`.
- `fn merge(mut self, a: MergeTree<D>, b: MergeTree<D>, leaf: (Z, Z, Z, Z) -> Z, pre_a: Z = Z.zero, pre_b: Z = Z.zero) -> MergeTree<D>` — \(O(\log \lvert D \rvert)\) amortized per `set`, over a sequence of merges whose results; The tree holding `leaf(a[x], b[x], pre_a, pre_b)` at each position `x`; it uses up `a` and `b`.

## Example

```cp
domain I = 0..4
var st = SegTree<I, Int>.of(+, i => Int(i) + 1)
st.set(I(2), 10)
print(st.fold(I(1)..=I(3)), st.all)
// output: 16 17
```
